rationale: Neuroimaging findings regarding anterior temporal lobe and external capsule involvement in autosomal recessive NOTCH3-related leukoencephalopathy (OMIM #621295) are directly contradictory in the literature. While a single case report (Ouskri et al., 2025) describes prominent anterior temporal lobe and external capsule hyperintensities mimicking CADASIL, multiple foundational cohort and case studies (Stellingwerff et al., 2022 [3/3 patients]; Tasharrofi et al., 2024 [1/1 patient]) explicitly document that the anterior temporal lobes are spared, noting this sparing as a key imaging discriminator separating recessive NOTCH3-associated arteriopathy/leukodystrophy from classic dominant CADASIL.

evidence.text: In a 12-year-old patient with a homozygous frameshift loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant presenting with recessive leukodystrophy, white matter hyperintensities were reported mainly involving the anterior temporal lobes and external capsules.

source.title: A novel homozygous loss-of-function NOTCH3 variant in a Moroccan patient: expanding the spectrum beyond CADASIL
source.quote: hyperintensities, mainly in anterior temporal lobes and external … early-onset arteriopathy and cavitating leukoencephalopathy

numbers.metric: anterior temporal and external capsule involvement

evidence.text: In three pediatric patients with early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy due to bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants, brain MRI showed extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities, basal ganglia lacunes, microbleeds, and microcalcifications, but the anterior temporal lobes were explicitly spared.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: The anterior temporal lobes were spared. Bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants in exons 1, 32, and 33 were found.

evidence.text: A proband with early-onset leukoencephalopathy homozygous for a NOTCH3 null variant exhibited white matter abnormalities on MRI without anterior temporal pole lesions, reinforcing observations across other recessive cases that anterior temporal pole abnormalities are typically absent.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed on a proband who exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions.

numbers.metric: patients lacking anterior temporal pole lesions

evidence.text: Classic CADASIL due to heterozygous NOTCH3 mutations typically displays white matter hyperintensities in the anterior temporal lobe and external capsule, which serve as hallmark markers distinguishing CADASIL from sporadic cerebral small vessel disease.

source.title: Update on the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and biomarkers of cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy
source.quote: Several characteristic features have been observed in the brain magnetic resonance images of patients with CADASIL, including subcortical lacunar lesions and white matter hyperintensities in the anterior temporal lobe or external capsule

conflicts: Ouskri et al. (2025) report that biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 leukodystrophy presents with white matter hyperintensities predominantly involving anterior temporal lobes and external capsules.
Stellingwerff et al. (2022) found that in 3 out of 3 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants, the anterior temporal lobes were strictly spared.

Tasharrofi et al. (2024) specifically highlighted that their biallelic NOTCH3 proband had white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions, matching earlier recessive cohorts rather than dominant CADASIL.

new_directions.question_text: Does anterior temporal lobe involvement in biallelic NOTCH3 disease correlate with specific variant classes (e.g., truncating frameshift/nonsense vs. cysteine-sparing missense) or disease duration/age?
new_directions.rationale: Differences in reported temporal pole lesions between Ouskri et al. (frameshift variant) and Stellingwerff et al. (cysteine-sparing variants in exons 1, 32, 33) suggest genotype-dependent neuroimaging divergence.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic sensitivity and specificity of temporal pole and external capsule hyperintensities across all published biallelic NOTCH3 cases compared to dominant CADASIL and CARASIL?
new_directions.rationale: A centralized, blinded neuroradiological re-review of all MRI series from published biallelic NOTCH3 patients will clarify whether anterior temporal pole involvement is truly an exception or an under-recognized progression marker.
